$comment: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how many integration checks each bundle must contain.
Read by scripts/assert-check-count.mjs (the coverage gate) and by test-harnesses/integration.mjs,
which uses `requires` to decide which bundles the default run should include on this host. Adding a
bundle means adding one row here and nowhere else; the number living in exactly one place is what
stops the gate and the suite from drifting into agreeing on a wrong figure.
`requires` names the sibling app a bundle needs. null means it always runs. A bundle whose app is
not linked is NOT expected to run, which is why a straight port of orders' gate would fail on a
sales-only host: it would demand bundles that cannot exist there.
NOTHING IS null ANY MORE, and that is a real change rather than tidying. Saving a deal provisions
its embedded order inside DealEntityServer.Save(), so a host without bizapps-orders cannot save a
deal at all -- and mj-app.json declares orders a hard dependency, which makes such a host
misconfigured rather than minimal. Leaving save-deal and close-deal marked null would have had the
gate demand two bundles that cannot pass there. The alternative -- gating provisioning on
OrdersIsInstalled() so a sales-only deal simply has no order -- was rejected in DECISIONS-NEEDED.md:
it trades a loud failure for a deal that is quietly missing the thing S-US4 says it must have.
Because no bundle is unconditional now, assert-check-count.mjs treats an EMPTY expectation as a
failure. Otherwise a run on a host with nothing linked would pass while executing zero checks --
the exact vacuous pass this file exists to prevent.
close-won-contract went from 4 to 1 on 2026-08-20 and back to `requires: null`. CT1-CT4 named
ContractTerm and ContractLine, which contracts deleted in its 2026-08-18 rebuild, and asserted a
Contract.Status column that no longer exists -- while being SKIPPED on every host, because contracts
is installed on none of them. Four claimed, zero delivered. CT0 replaces them: it asserts contracts
is ABSENT, so it runs everywhere and goes red the day that stops being true, naming what to write.
`count` is the number of checks REGISTERED in the bundle, not the number that ran. The gate compares
both, because the interesting failure is a bundle that registers 4 and runs 0.

close-won-contract.ids: CT1, CT4, CT5, CT6 — the CT0 tripwire fired twice and is retired; CT2/CT3 unwritable after the v2 rebuild

$comment_close_won_tasks: 12, AND THE TRANSIENT STATE THAT MADE THIS NUMBER ODD IS NOW RESOLVED -- it resolved exactly here.
Two sessions each added an eleventh check to this bundle. WT1-WT10 were shared; the integrated
branch added WT11 (a LOST close raises no tasks) and the tasks branch added what was also called
WT11 (the task-type lookup column), renamed to WT12 before merging. Neither branch had both, so
the tasks branch deliberately set 12 while registering 11 and let its own gate read 11-of-12 --
on the reasoning that 11 would have been green on the branch and silently wrong the moment it
merged, and the silently-wrong version is the one nobody notices. That call was right and this
merge is what closes it: 12 registered, 12 expected.
Kept as history rather than deleted, because the next person to face a two-branch count collision
should be able to find the reasoning rather than re-derive it.
